comment: Google API surfaces that mint, exchange or export a reusable credential.
ADR 0109 gives a session a short-lived, policy-bound access token. A guest
that can reach any surface below can trade that token for a credential the
proxy no longer bounds — a longer-lived token, a downscoped token for a
different service account, or an exportable service-account key. None of
these is ever a guest surface, whatever endpoint an administrator selects.
This file is the ONE source for both enforcement points: the Rust egress
proxy include_str!s it, and the orchestrator imports it to validate the
endpoints an administrator configures. Before this file the two lists were
written by hand and had already drifted — the orchestrator knew four hosts,
the proxy knew five, and neither knew the .mtls variants.
Matching (see google_denylist.rs):
- The host is normalized first: lowercased, a trailing dot removed, and
an `.mtls` label dropped, so sts.mtls.googleapis.com == sts.googleapis.com.
- `denied_hosts` entries are exact hosts or a `*.suffix` wildcard. A match
rejects the connection at admission, before any TLS, so a bypass
(non-intercepted) connection is covered too.
- `denied_operations` entries match a request. Every matcher family listed
on a rule must hit; an omitted family is no constraint. Paths are
compared after the query is dropped and percent escapes are decoded, and
are written in lower case.

denied_operations.why: IAM Credentials REST verbs. Regional and transcoded routes serve them under other googleapis hosts, so the host is a wildcard.
The same verbs over gRPC. A gRPC request carries the service and method in the path, which the REST shapes above never match.
The OAuth token endpoint on the legacy discovery host.
Service-account key creation exports a private key that outlives the session.
The v1 shape of the same operation.
Identity Platform sign-in returns a refresh token.
